page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.small is an entry-level virtual machine instance within the shared family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It is provisioned with 1 shared vCPU (1 physical core and 1 thread), paired with 2.0 GB of memory. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying processor supports instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Hardware bundling is minimal for this instance size. The ecs.n4.small includes no dedicated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data. It features no hardware GPU accelerators and lists a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. Memory throughput measures 8.61 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 7.28 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while small-block cached reads reach 79.26 GB/sec.

Benchmark results place the instance in the lower performance brackets due to its single shared vCPU configuration. It yields a stress-ng score of 1061.69 in both single-core and multi-core evaluations, placing it in the bottom 25 percent for single-core and bottom 10 percent for multi-core. PassMark scores reflect similar trends, with a CPU score of 1277.65 and a memory score of 712.83. The instance processes static web traffic at 1.22 GB/sec and handles 1.22 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation, minimal 2.0 GB memory footprint, and absence of local storage, ecs.n4.small offers low baseline resource costs at the expense of computational performance and sustained throughput. The instance is suited for non-critical, lightweight workloads such as basic development and testing, low-traffic web serving, microservices, and modest background utility tasks.
